claim: Nrxn1,2,3α transcripts are expressed in cornus ammonis (CA) pyramidal cells in mouse hippocampus.
source: Similar to what has been reported for rat hippocampus (Ullrich et al., 1995) we find significant expression of Nrxn1,2,3α transcripts in cornus ammonis (CA) pyramidal cells as well as presumptive interneurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B, and is also supported by citation to previous work in rat hippocampus.

claim: Nrxn1,2,3α transcripts are expressed in presumptive interneurons in mouse hippocampus.
source: Similar to what has been reported for rat hippocampus (Ullrich et al., 1995) we find significant expression of Nrxn1,2,3α transcripts in cornus ammonis (CA) pyramidal cells as well as presumptive interneurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B, and is also supported by citation to previous work in rat hippocampus.

claim: Nrxn1,2,3 mRNAs are recovered in CamK2Ribo transcript preparations.
source: Nrxn1,2,3 mRNAs were recovered in both CamK2Ribo and PVRibo cell-derived transcript preparations (note that Nrxn3β expression in mouse hippocampus is low and could not be reliably detected – see Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RiboTrap purification data shown in Figure 1C and related supplementary figures.

claim: Nrxn1,2,3 mRNAs are recovered in PVRibo transcript preparations.
source: Nrxn1,2,3 mRNAs were recovered in both CamK2Ribo and PVRibo cell-derived transcript preparations (note that Nrxn3β expression in mouse hippocampus is low and could not be reliably detected – see Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RiboTrap purification data shown in Figure 1C and related supplementary figures.

claim: Nrxn3β expression in mouse hippocampus is low and could not be reliably detected.
source: Nrxn1,2,3 mRNAs were recovered in both CamK2Ribo and PVRibo cell-derived transcript preparations (note that Nrxn3β expression in mouse hippocampus is low and could not be reliably detected – see Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C demonstrating low expression levels.

claim: Nrxn3α is most highly enriched in the PV-cell population amongst all neurexin transcripts.
source: Notably, amongst all neurexin transcripts Nrxn3α was most highly enriched in the PV-cell population (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C comparing enrichment of different neurexin transcripts in PVRibo preparations.

claim: PV-cell expression of Nrxn3α is confirmed by dual labeling with in situ hybridization and immunostaining in Pvalbcre::Ai9Tom mice.
source: PV-cell expression of Nrxn3α was further confirmed by dual labeling with in situ hybridization using Nrxn3α probes and immunostaining in mice where PV+ cells were genetically labelled with red fluorescent protein (Pvalbcre::Ai9Tom) (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by dual labeling data shown in Figure 1D combining in situ hybridization and genetic labeling.

claim: The alternative exon at AS4 is largely skipped in CamK2Ribo cells.
source: While in CamK2Ribo cells the cassette exon at AS4 was largely skipped there was a high level of alternative exon inclusion in PVRibo cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by radioactive PCR data shown in Figure 2B and C demonstrating differential splicing patterns.

claim: There is a high level of alternative exon inclusion at AS4 in PVRibo cells.
source: While in CamK2Ribo cells the cassette exon at AS4 was largely skipped there was a high level of alternative exon inclusion in PVRibo cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by radioactive PCR data shown in Figure 2B and C demonstrating differential splicing patterns.

claim: Alternative exon incorporation rates at AS4 are divergent between CamK2Ribo and PVRibo cell populations for all three Nrxn transcripts (Nrxn1,2,3).
source: Moreover, for all three Nrxn transcripts (Nrxn1,2,3) the alternative exon incorporation rates at AS4 were remarkably divergent between the two cell populations (Figure 2B and C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by radioactive PCR data shown in Figure 2B and C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Nrxn1 AS6 exhibits differential usage in PV− versus CamK2 cells.
source: Interestingly, Nrxn1 AS6 and Nrxn2 AS2 exhibited differential usage in PV− versus CamK2 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by radioactive PCR data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Nrxn2 AS2 exhibits differential usage in PV− versus CamK2 cells.
source: Interestingly, Nrxn1 AS6 and Nrxn2 AS2 exhibited differential usage in PV− versus CamK2 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by radioactive PCR data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: More than 90% of CamK2Ribo-positive cells are Slm2-positive.
source: As reported previously (Stoss et al., 2004; Iijima et al., 2014), we observed high expression of Slm2 protein in pyramidal cells, and more than 90% of CamK2Ribo-positive cells were Slm2-positive (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2E and is consistent with previous reports.

claim: 75% of cells marked in Pvalbcre::Ai9Tom mice in hippocampus area CA1 do not express Slm2.
source: By contrast, 75% of cells marked in Pvalbcre::Ai9Tom mice in hippocampus area CA1 do not express Slm2 (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2E quantifying Slm2 expression in genetically labeled PV+ cells.

claim: Cells within or close to the pyramidal cell layer in Pvalbcre::Ai9Tom mice are Slm2-negative.
source: In particular, cells within or close to the pyramidal cell layer were Slm2-negative (Figure 2D and E - note that the percentage of Slm2-expressing 'PV+ cells' depends on the anatomical position within the hippocampus and the use of genetic versus antibody-labeling to define 'PV+ cells', Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Slm2 transcripts are enriched in the CamK2Ribo population.
source: Consistent with the immunohistochemistry results, we observed an enrichment of Slm2 transcripts in the CamK2Ribo population and a de-enrichment in the PVRibo preparations (similarly the Slm2 paralogues Slm1 and Sam68 were de-enriched).
evidence: The claim is supported by real-time qPCR data shown in Figure 2F on polysome-associated transcripts.

claim: Slm2 transcripts are de-enriched in the PVRibo preparations.
source: Consistent with the immunohistochemistry results, we observed an enrichment of Slm2 transcripts in the CamK2Ribo population and a de-enrichment in the PVRibo preparations (similarly the Slm2 paralogues Slm1 and Sam68 were de-enriched).
evidence: The claim is supported by real-time qPCR data shown in Figure 2F on polysome-associated transcripts.

claim: Slm1 transcripts are de-enriched in the PVRibo preparations.
source: Consistent with the immunohistochemistry results, we observed an enrichment of Slm2 transcripts in the CamK2Ribo population and a de-enrichment in the PVRibo preparations (similarly the Slm2 paralogues Slm1 and Sam68 were de-enriched).
evidence: The claim is supported by real-time qPCR data shown in Figure 2F on polysome-associated transcripts.

claim: Sam68 transcripts are de-enriched in the PVRibo preparations.
source: Consistent with the immunohistochemistry results, we observed an enrichment of Slm2 transcripts in the CamK2Ribo population and a de-enrichment in the PVRibo preparations (similarly the Slm2 paralogues Slm1 and Sam68 were de-enriched).
evidence: The claim is supported by real-time qPCR data shown in Figure 2F on polysome-associated transcripts.

claim: Global ablation of Slm2 results in a significant loss of the skipped (AS4-) neurexin isoforms.
source: Given that global ablation of Slm2 results in a significant loss of the skipped (AS4-) neurexin isoforms (Ehrmann et al., 2013; Traunmüller et al., 2014), this strongly suggests that differential expression of Slm2 in pyramidal versus PV+ cells drives the cell type-specific skipping of alternative exons at AS4 in pyramidal cells of the hippocampus.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Ehrmann et al., 2013; Traunmüller et al., 2014) demonstrating the effect of Slm2 ablation.

claim: Differential expression of Slm2 in pyramidal versus PV+ cells drives the cell type-specific skipping of alternative exons at AS4 in pyramidal cells of the hippocampus.
source: Given that global ablation of Slm2 results in a significant loss of the skipped (AS4-) neurexin isoforms (Ehrmann et al., 2013; Traunmüller et al., 2014), this strongly suggests that differential expression of Slm2 in pyramidal versus PV+ cells drives the cell type-specific skipping of alternative exons at AS4 in pyramidal cells of the hippocampus.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the differential expression of Slm2 and its known role in AS4 splicing regulation.

claim: Ectopic expression of Slm2 in cerebellar granule cells is sufficient to shift alternative splicing in favor of Nrxn AS4- isoforms.
source: Finally, we observed that ectopic expression of Slm2 in cells that normally do not express high levels of STAR proteins (cerebellar granule cells in culture) was sufficient to shift alternative splicing in favor of Nrxn AS4- isoforms (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 demonstrating the effect of Slm2 overexpression.

claim: Cbln4-encoding transcripts are enriched in the PV+ cell population.
source: We detected an enrichment of Cbln4-encoding transcripts in the PV+ cell population (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A from PVRibo preparations.

claim: The CamK2Ribo population is de-enriched for Cbln2 transcripts.
source: By contrast, the CamK2Ribo population was de-enriched for both, Cbln2 and Cbln4 transcripts (note that Cbln1 and Cbln3 show very low expression in the mouse hippocampus as compared to the cerebellum, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A from CamK2Ribo preparations.

claim: The CamK2Ribo population is de-enriched for Cbln4 transcripts.
source: By contrast, the CamK2Ribo population was de-enriched for both, Cbln2 and Cbln4 transcripts (note that Cbln1 and Cbln3 show very low expression in the mouse hippocampus as compared to the cerebellum, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A from CamK2Ribo preparations.

claim: Cbln1 shows very low expression in the mouse hippocampus as compared to the cerebellum.
source: By contrast, the CamK2Ribo population was de-enriched for both, Cbln2 and Cbln4 transcripts (note that Cbln1 and Cbln3 show very low expression in the mouse hippocampus as compared to the cerebellum, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A comparing expression in hippocampus and cerebellum.

claim: Cbln3 shows very low expression in the mouse hippocampus as compared to the cerebellum.
source: By contrast, the CamK2Ribo population was de-enriched for both, Cbln2 and Cbln4 transcripts (note that Cbln1 and Cbln3 show very low expression in the mouse hippocampus as compared to the cerebellum, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A comparing expression in hippocampus and cerebellum.

claim: Cbln4 binds to cells expressing Nrx1α AS4+.
source: Using in vitro binding assays with Cbln4 from conditioned media we confirmed binding to cells expressing Nrx1α AS4+ but significantly lower binding to Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3B–D.

claim: Cbln4 shows significantly lower binding to Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms compared to Nrx1α AS4+.
source: Using in vitro binding assays with Cbln4 from conditioned media we confirmed binding to cells expressing Nrx1α AS4+ but significantly lower binding to Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3B–D.

claim: Cbln1 is strongly retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln1 together with Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms.
source: In this assay, Cbln1 or 4 were strongly retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln1 or Cbln4 together with Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms but not Nrx3 AS4- (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell surface retention assay data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Cbln4 is strongly retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln4 together with Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms.
source: In this assay, Cbln1 or 4 were strongly retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln1 or Cbln4 together with Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms but not Nrx3 AS4- (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell surface retention assay data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Cbln1 is not retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln1 together with Nrx3 AS4- isoforms.
source: In this assay, Cbln1 or 4 were strongly retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln1 or Cbln4 together with Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms but not Nrx3 AS4- (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell surface retention assay data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Cbln4 is not retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln4 together with Nrx3 AS4- isoforms.
source: In this assay, Cbln1 or 4 were strongly retained at the cell surface of cells co-expressing Cbln1 or Cbln4 together with Nrx3 AS4+ isoforms but not Nrx3 AS4- (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell surface retention assay data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Cbln4 associates with Nrx3α proteins in a AS4 splice-isoform-specific manner.
source: Thus, Cbln4 indeed associates not only with Nrx1α but also Nrx3α proteins in a AS4 splice-isoform-specific manner (further studies will be required to confirm whether these interactions are direct or whether they may involve additional linker proteins).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the cell surface retention assay data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Inclusion of the 30 amino acid AS4+ insertion elevates the action of Nrx3α proteins towards GABAergic postsynaptic sites.
source: Inclusion of the 30 amino acid AS4+ insertion elevated the action of Nrx3α proteins towards GABAergic postsynaptic sites (Figure 3H and I and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C. Note that for Nrx1α we did not observe the same impact of the AS4+ insertions, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by heterologous cell assay data shown in Figure 3H and I.

claim: For Nrx1α, the AS4+ insertion does not have the same impact on synaptogenic activity as observed for Nrx3α.
source: Inclusion of the 30 amino acid AS4+ insertion elevated the action of Nrx3α proteins towards GABAergic postsynaptic sites (Figure 3H and I and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C. Note that for Nrx1α we did not observe the same impact of the AS4+ insertions, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by heterologous cell assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: Co-expression of Cbln4 with Nrx isoforms neither enhances nor inhibits the synaptogenic activity in heterologous cell assays.
source: Co-expression of Cbln4 with the Nrx isoforms neither enhanced nor inhibited the synaptogenic activity in this assay (Figure 3H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by heterologous cell assay data shown in Figure 3H and I.

claim: Germline ablation of Nrxn3 exon 21 results in a complete loss of exon 21-containing Nrxn3 transcripts.
source: Upon germline ablation we observed a complete loss of exon 21-containing Nrxn3 transcripts (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by PCR analysis data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Loss of Nrx3 AS4+ protein isoforms in Nrxn3ex21Δ mice is confirmed by serial reaction monitoring mass-spectrometry assays.
source: Loss of Nrx3 AS4+ protein isoforms was confirmed by serial reaction monitoring mass-spectrometry assays (Schreiner et al., 2015) designed to specifically quantify expression of AS4+ isoforms (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Alternative splicing in Nrxn1 and 2 is unchanged in Nrxn3ex21Δ mice.
source: Importantly, alternative splicing in Nrxn1 and 2 as well as total Nrx1,2,3 protein levels were unchanged (Figure 4B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 4B and D.

claim: Total Nrx1,2,3 protein levels are unchanged in Nrxn3ex21Δ mice.
source: Importantly, alternative splicing in Nrxn1 and 2 as well as total Nrx1,2,3 protein levels were unchanged (Figure 4B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The Nrxn3 exon 21 mutation specifically alters the splice isoform identity but not total protein or transcript neurexin levels in the hippocampus.
source: Thus, the Nrxn3 exon 21 mutation specifically alters the splice isoform identity but not total protein or transcript neurexin levels in the hippocampus.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data shown in Figure 4B and D demonstrating unchanged total levels but altered splicing.

claim: Nrxn3ex21ΔPV single mutant mice are born at Mendelian ratios.
source: The conditional Nrxn3ex21ΔPV single mutant mice and Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV double mutant mice were born at Mendelian ratios and were viable and fertile (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV double mutant mice are born at Mendelian ratios.
source: The conditional Nrxn3ex21ΔPV single mutant mice and Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV double mutant mice were born at Mendelian ratios and were viable and fertile (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nrxn3ex21ΔPV single mutant mice are viable and fertile.
source: The conditional Nrxn3ex21ΔPV single mutant mice and Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV double mutant mice were born at Mendelian ratios and were viable and fertile (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV double mutant mice are viable and fertile.
source: The conditional Nrxn3ex21ΔPV single mutant mice and Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV double mutant mice were born at Mendelian ratios and were viable and fertile (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overall hippocampal anatomy is not detectably changed in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: Overall, hippocampal anatomy and density of PV-immunoreactive cells was not detectably changed, indicating that the mutations did not result in severe developmental defects (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Density of PV-immunoreactive cells is not detectably changed in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: Overall, hippocampal anatomy and density of PV-immunoreactive cells was not detectably changed, indicating that the mutations did not result in severe developmental defects (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The mutations did not result in severe developmental defects.
source: Overall, hippocampal anatomy and density of PV-immunoreactive cells was not detectably changed, indicating that the mutations did not result in severe developmental defects (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the unchanged hippocampal anatomy and PV+ cell density.

claim: There is no change in the density of perisomatic synapses detected by immunostaining for Neuroligin2 in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: In the conditional single and double knock-out mice there was no change in the density of perisomatic synapses detected by immunostaining for the postsynaptic GABAergic marker Neuroligin2 (NL2) and synaptotagmin2 (Syt2) (which selectively marks PV+ cell terminals [Sommeijer and Levelt, 2012]) (Figure 5A and B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A and B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: There is no change in the density of perisomatic synapses detected by immunostaining for synaptotagmin2 in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: In the conditional single and double knock-out mice there was no change in the density of perisomatic synapses detected by immunostaining for the postsynaptic GABAergic marker Neuroligin2 (NL2) and synaptotagmin2 (Syt2) (which selectively marks PV+ cell terminals [Sommeijer and Levelt, 2012]) (Figure 5A and B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A and B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Synaptotagmin2 selectively marks PV+ cell terminals.
source: In the conditional single and double knock-out mice there was no change in the density of perisomatic synapses detected by immunostaining for the postsynaptic GABAergic marker Neuroligin2 (NL2) and synaptotagmin2 (Syt2) (which selectively marks PV+ cell terminals [Sommeijer and Levelt, 2012]) (Figure 5A and B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sommeijer and Levelt, 2012.

claim: There is no change in inhibitory synapses formed between PV+ interneurons in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: Moreover, we did not detect any change in inhibitory synapses formed between PV+ interneurons as identified as Syt2-positive structures formed onto PV+ somata (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ultrastructure of perisomatic PV+ interneuron output synapses formed onto pyramidal cells is unaltered in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: The ultrastructure of perisomatic PV+ interneurons output synapses formed onto pyramidal cells (identified based on location and ultrastructural characteristics [Takács et al., 2015]) was unaltered in the conditional single and double knock-out mice (Figure 5C–F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5C–F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: Frequency of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents (mIPSCs) recorded from CA1 neurons is unchanged in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: Moreover, frequency and amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents (mIPSCs) recorded from CA1 neurons in conditional single and double knock-out mice were unchanged (Figure 5G and H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5G and H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: Amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents (mIPSCs) recorded from CA1 neurons is unchanged in conditional single and double knock-out mice.
source: Moreover, frequency and amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents (mIPSCs) recorded from CA1 neurons in conditional single and double knock-out mice were unchanged (Figure 5G and H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5G and H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: Basal inhibitory synaptic transmission in CA1 pyramidal cells is not severely affected by ablation of PV-cell specific Nrxn1 and Nrxn3 AS4+ isoforms.
source: These findings indicate that basal inhibitory synaptic transmission in the CA1 pyramidal cells and synaptic structure are not severely affected by the ablation of the PV-cell specific Nrxn1 and Nrxn3 AS4+ isoforms.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the unchanged mIPSC frequency and amplitude data.

claim: Synaptic structure is not severely affected by ablation of PV-cell specific Nrxn1 and Nrxn3 AS4+ isoforms.
source: These findings indicate that basal inhibitory synaptic transmission in the CA1 pyramidal cells and synaptic structure are not severely affected by the ablation of the PV-cell specific Nrxn1 and Nrxn3 AS4+ isoforms.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the unchanged ultrastructural and synaptic marker data.

claim: There is a significant elevation in the density of c-fos+ cells in CA3 regions of Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice.
source: These experiments revealed a significant elevation in the density of c-fos+ cells in CA3 regions of the Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice (Figure 6B), indicating that network activity is elevated upon ablation of the PV-cell-specific Nrxn splice insertions.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Network activity is elevated upon ablation of the PV-cell-specific Nrxn splice insertions.
source: These experiments revealed a significant elevation in the density of c-fos+ cells in CA3 regions of the Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice (Figure 6B), indicating that network activity is elevated upon ablation of the PV-cell-specific Nrxn splice insertions.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the increased c-fos+ cell density, which is a marker of neuronal activity.

claim: Control mice exhibit a significant preference for exploring novel over familiar objects in the novel object recognition task.
source: In this task, control mice exhibit a significant preference for exploring novel over familiar objects.
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mutant mice spent equal time exploring familiar and novel objects in the novel object recognition task.
source: By contrast, we observed that Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mutant mice spent equal time exploring familiar and novel objects, indicating a defect in short-term memory (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mutant mice have a defect in short-term memory.
source: By contrast, we observed that Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mutant mice spent equal time exploring familiar and novel objects, indicating a defect in short-term memory (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the lack of preference for novel objects in the behavioral task.

claim: Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice show similar total object exploration times as control mice.
source: These defects were not a consequence of general behavioral disruptions as the mice showed similar total object exploration times, normal locomotion, and no signs of anxiety-related behaviors (Figure 6E–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice show normal locomotion.
source: These defects were not a consequence of general behavioral disruptions as the mice showed similar total object exploration times, normal locomotion, and no signs of anxiety-related behaviors (Figure 6E–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6F–H.

claim: Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice show no signs of anxiety-related behaviors.
source: These defects were not a consequence of general behavioral disruptions as the mice showed similar total object exploration times, normal locomotion, and no signs of anxiety-related behaviors (Figure 6E–K).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6I–K.

claim: PV-cell-specific loss of Nrxn1 and 3 AS4+ splice variants results in impairment in neuronal circuit function.
source: Thus, PV-cell-specific loss of Nrxn1 and 3 AS4+ splice variants results in impairment in neuronal circuit function.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the increased c-fos expression and behavioral deficits observed in the conditional knock-out mice.

claim: Neurexin alpha triple knock-out mice show a 40% reduction in the density of presumptive inhibitory synapses.
source: Global knock-out studies demonstrated that neurexin alpha triple knock-out mice show a 40% reduction in the density of presumptive inhibitory synapses and defects in synaptic transmission in the brain stem of perinatal mice (Missler et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Missler et al., 2003.

claim: Neurexin alpha triple knock-out mice show defects in synaptic transmission in the brain stem of perinatal mice.
source: Global knock-out studies demonstrated that neurexin alpha triple knock-out mice show a 40% reduction in the density of presumptive inhibitory synapses and defects in synaptic transmission in the brain stem of perinatal mice (Missler et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Missler et al., 2003.

claim: Simultaneous global ablation of all Nrxn3 transcripts results in brain area-specific alterations in synaptic transmission.
source: Moreover, simultaneous global ablation of all Nrxn3 transcripts results in brain area-specifc alterations in synaptic transmission (Aoto et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Aoto et al., 2015.

claim: Pyramidal and PV+ cells share primary Nrxn1,2,3 transcripts.
source: The data presented here demonstrate that pyramidal and PV+ cells share primary Nrxn1,2,3 transcripts but that the endogenous neurexin isoforms differ dramatically in their alternative splicing regulation at AS4.
evidence: The claim is supported by RiboTrap purification data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Endogenous neurexin isoforms in pyramidal and PV+ cells differ dramatically in their alternative splicing regulation at AS4.
source: The data presented here demonstrate that pyramidal and PV+ cells share primary Nrxn1,2,3 transcripts but that the endogenous neurexin isoforms differ dramatically in their alternative splicing regulation at AS4.
evidence: The claim is supported by radioactive PCR data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: The increased c-fos+ expression in the hippocampus of Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice indicates that the AS4+ isoforms have important functions.
source: Regardless, the increased c-fos+ expression in the hippocampus of Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice indicates that the AS4+ isoforms have important functions and presumably reflects an impairment in PV+ cell mediated inhibition in hippocampal circuits.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the c-fos expression data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The increased c-fos+ expression in the hippocampus of Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice presumably reflects an impairment in PV+ cell mediated inhibition in hippocampal circuits.
source: Regardless, the increased c-fos+ expression in the hippocampus of Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice indicates that the AS4+ isoforms have important functions and presumably reflects an impairment in PV+ cell mediated inhibition in hippocampal circuits.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on the c-fos expression data and the known role of PV+ cells in inhibition.

claim: The impairment of short-term memory in Nrxn1/3ex21ΔPV mice supports the notion that neurexin AS4+ isoforms have important functions in the cells targeted by the Pvalbcre line in the hippocampus.
source: Moreover, the impairment of short-term memory further supports the notion that neurexin AS4+ isoforms have important functions in the cells targeted by the Pvalbcre line in the hippocampus.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the behavioral data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: Dysfunction of PV+ interneuron networks has been postulated to be a major contributor to the pathophysiology of schizophrenia and autism.
source: Dysfunction of PV+ interneuron networks has been postulated to be a major contributor to the pathophysiology of schizophrenia and autism (Del Pino et al., 2013; Gogolla et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Del Pino et al., 2013 and Gogolla et al., 2014.

claim: Part of the neuronal circuit deficits resulting from Nrxn1 and 3 mutations in disease states may directly impair output synapses of the PV-interneuron network.
source: Thus, we speculate that part of the neuronal circuit deficits resulting from Nrxn1 and 3 mutations in disease states may directly impair output synapses of the PV-interneuron network.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on the findings in the conditional knock-out mice and the known association of neurexin mutations with disease.

claim: Neurexins (Nrxn1,2,3) represent one gene family of highly diversified synaptic adhesion molecules.
